parts: Do people actually check the sources an AI answer cites?

props.text: Rarely, and the citations often would not hold up. In an audit of generative search engines, only about half of the generated sentences were fully supported by their citations.

props.label: arxiv.org
props.title: Evaluating verifiability in generative search engines
props.description: Liu, Zhang and Liang (2023): about half of generated sentences fully supported, and a quarter of citations not supporting their sentence.

props.text: The marks still raise trust, even when the citations are random.

props.label: arxiv.org
props.title: Citations and trust in LLM generated responses
props.description: Ding et al. (AAAI 2025): trust rises with citations present, whether or not they are relevant, and falls when people check them.

props.text: Few follow them: links inside Google’s AI summaries are clicked on about 1% of visits.

props.label: pewresearch.org
props.title: Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears
props.description: Pew Research Center (2025): a link inside the summary was clicked on 1% of visits that showed one.
